articles.title: Despite 69 Criminal Charges Involving Secret Recordings of Adults and Children in County Park Restroom, Hollywood Man Not Arrested
articles.description: UPDATE 11/22/2026: Richard Allen Lehman, 58, of Hollywood, is facing 69 misdemeanor charges in connection with an investigation into allegations that he secretly recorded adults and children inside a men's restroom at Chancellors Run Regional Park during Little League Opening Day activities in April 2026. The latest charges were filed November 10, 2026, following an earlier filing of 18 misdemeanor charges against Lehman on August 17, 2026. However, the original criminal case no longer appears in Maryland Judiciary Case Search, and it remains unclear whether those earlier charges were dismissed, withdrawn, replaced, or otherwise resolved. The 69 charges in the newer case are confirmed, but the status of the original 18 charges has not been established. The latest charges include 23 counts of conducting visual surveillance in a private place with prurient intent, 23 counts of using a camera to record another person's private area without consent and with prurient intent, and 23 counts involving the alleged preparation of obscene video material. According to St. Mary's County Sheriff's Office Detective Corporal David M. Lawrence, investigators recovered 12 additional videos from Lehman's Motorola smartphone that allegedly depicted nine additional adults and five additional children using the restroom without their knowledge or consent. Combined with the six individuals identified during the original investigation, the allegations now involve at least 20 people, including seven juveniles. Several individuals remain unidentified, but investigators consulted with the St. Mary's County State's Attorney's Office and determined that charges could still be pursued. The additional allegations substantially expand the original investigation, which initially involved four adults and two juvenile males. Investigators previously reported that one of the juveniles appeared in four separate recordings. The newly identified footage allegedly captured additional restroom users, including children, who were unaware they were being recorded. The 23 counts in each of the three new charge categories reflect separate allegations, with multiple charges involving the same underlying investigation. The newer filing also raises questions about a discrepancy involving the date of the alleged incident. While the original 18 charges listed April 13, 2026, as the offense date, all 69 new charges identify April 11, 2026. That date is consistent with the Little League Opening Day ceremonies and the St. Mary's County Sheriff's Office's original public announcement regarding suspicious restroom activity at the park. The available filings do not explain why the earlier charges listed a different date. Rather than issuing an arrest warrant, the court issued Lehman a criminal summons on November 10, 2026. An updated docket entry filed November 17, 2026, confirms that the summons was officially served. Lehman was found eligible for representation by the Office of the Public Defender on November 13, 2026, and a public defender formally entered an appearance on his behalf November 16, 2026. That same day, his defense filed a request for a speedy trial and demanded access to the prosecution's evidence. A preliminary inquiry originally scheduled for December 18, 2026, at 1 p.m. in St. Mary's County District Court was canceled after the proceeding was waived. The cancellation does not mean the criminal charges were dismissed. The newer case remains open, and no trial date has been listed in the available information. The next court proceedings have not yet been announced. All 69 charges in the newer filing are misdemeanors. The surveillance-related offenses carry potential penalties of up to one year in jail and a $2,500 fine per count, while the obscene-material offenses carry potential penalties of up to one year in jail and a $1,000 fine per count. Although Lehman was initially charged in August 2026 and subsequently faced the expanded charges in November 2026, the disappearance of the earlier case from public Case Search results leaves the status of those original charges unresolved. Lehman is presumed innocent of the allegations unless and until proven guilty in court. 8/19/2026: Richard Allen Lehman, 58, of Hollywood, is facing 18 misdemeanor charges after investigators alleged he secretly recorded six people, including two juvenile males, inside a men's restroom at Chancellors Run Regional Park in Great Mills during Little League Opening Day activities in April 2026. The charges were not filed until August 17, 2026, more than four months after the alleged incident. A criminal summons was issued for Lehman rather than an arrest warrant, and as of 2:20 p.m. on August 19, 2026, the available information did not show that the summons had been served. Lehman is charged with six counts of Peeping Tom, six counts of conducting visual surveillance in a private place with prurient intent, and six counts of using a camera to conduct visual surveillance of a person's private area with prurient intent. The St. Mary's County Sheriff's Office had publicly acknowledged the investigation months before charges were filed. In an April 11, 2026 news release, the agency said deputies working security for St. Mary's Little League Opening Day ceremonies responded at approximately 9 a.m. to reports of a man engaging in suspicious behavior inside a restroom at Chancellors Run Regional Park in Great Mills. The Sheriff's Office said one person was detained and that the Criminal Investigations Division was handling the investigation. The agency asked anyone who witnessed suspicious activity or had additional information to contact Detective Andrew Burgess. The release did not identify the person who was detained. The St. Mary's County Sheriff's Office initially reported the incident occurred during Little League Opening Day on April 11, 2026. St. Mary's Little League's official schedule also confirms Opening Day was April 11. However, the filings against Lehman list April 13, 2026, as the offense date for all 18 charges. The reason for the discrepancy is not explained in the filings. According to allegations later filed by the St. Mary's County Sheriff's Office, patrol officers were working a part-time security assignment at Chancellors Run Regional Park for the 2026 Little League Opening Day ceremonies when an off-duty Maryland State Police master trooper used the men's restroom and entered the second toilet stall. The dividers between the stalls did not extend completely to the ground. While inside the stall, the trooper noticed a person in the first stall with his pants or shorts pulled down and a cellphone hanging from his left pocket. The trooper believed the phone had been deliberately positioned and angled toward the adjoining stall in a manner consistent with secretly recording someone. While inside, the trooper noticed a person in the first stall with his pants or shorts pulled down and a cellphone hanging from his left pocket. The trooper believed the phone had been deliberately positioned and angled toward the adjoining stall in a manner consistent with secretly recording someone. The trooper reported first noticing the same person in the restroom shortly after arriving at the park. About an hour later, he escorted a juvenile male into the restroom. After the juvenile left the stall, the trooper said he could see the same person's pants and cellphone in nearly the same position he had observed earlier. When the man exited the restroom, the trooper identified himself as a police officer. Authorities said the man was identified through his Maryland driver's license as Lehman. Patrol officers asked Lehman whether he had any cellphones on him. According to investigators, Lehman removed a blue Apple iPhone from his pocket. The trooper told officers that was not the phone he had seen hanging from the pocket inside the restroom. Lehman then retrieved a black Motorola Android smartphone from another pocket, according to the allegations. Officers seized both phones. St. Mary's County Sheriff's Office D/Cpl. David M. Lawrence later sought a search warrant for the Motorola phone. The warrant was authorized by Judge A. Lorenzini. Lawrence reported that investigators recovered numerous videos from the Motorola that allegedly had been recorded from inside the men's restroom at Chancellors Run Regional Park. Investigators identified six alleged victims, including four adults and two juvenile males. Their names are being withheld to protect their privacy. Authorities alleged that none of them knew they were being recorded or had consented to the recordings. One of the juvenile victims was allegedly captured in four separate videos. Investigators said the recordings showed the alleged victims using the restroom with various parts of their bodies exposed. The two juvenile males were allegedly recorded while sitting on a toilet, with the side of their buttocks visible. The six Peeping Tom charges allege Lehman conducted visual surveillance of another person in a private place without that person's consent. Each count carries a listed maximum penalty of 30 days in jail, a $1,000 fine, or both. The six private-place surveillance charges allege that Lehman conducted visual surveillance with prurient intent and without consent. The six additional camera-surveillance charges allege that he used a camera to record a person's private area with prurient intent and without consent. Each of those counts carries a listed maximum penalty of one year in jail, a $2,500 fine, or both.

pendingReview.title: Police investigating suspected voyeurism at Vancouver elementary school
pendingReview.description: Police in Vancouver are investigating after a man allegedly engaged in voyeurism at a local elementary school. Vancouver police say it happened on Tuesday at a school in the area of Main Street and East 33rd Avenue. They say a 12-year-old girl reported to the school's liaison officer that the student was in a stall in the girl's bathroom when an unknown man "peered over the divider." The student reported screaming and running out to get help, and she is now receiving support from Vancouver police's victim services. The suspect fled the scene and has not been located, and police have released images and a video of the man in hopes of spurring public help in identifying him. Police say the man is not believed to be connected to the community of the school, but it has not been completely ruled out.

pendingReview.title: Vancouver police seek suspect after voyeurism incident at elementary school
pendingReview.description: Police are asking for the public's help to identify a suspect after an alleged incident of voyeurism at an East Vancouver elementary school. The Vancouver Police Department says a school liaison officer was called to General Brock Elementary School near Main Street and East 33rd Avenue around 1:30 p.m. Tuesday to meet with a 12-year-old girl and her guardian. "According to the report, the student was in a stall in the girls' washroom after lunch, believing she was alone, when an unknown man peered over the divider," police wrote in a statement Friday. "The student screamed and ran out of the washroom, and the man fled the school." Police say the do not believe the man is connected to the school community, but that possibility has not been completely ruled out. The department has released images and video of the suspect in hopes of identifying him. The VPD says it is working with the Vancouver School Board to support the student and broader school community as the investigation continues. Anyone who recognizes the suspect is asked to call the VPD at 604-717-0614.

pendingReview.description: The Vancouver Police Department (VPD) is seeking help from the public to identify a man who is suspected of voyeurism at a Vancouver elementary school. On Nov. 24, around 1:30 p.m., a Vancouver Police School Liaison Officer was called to an elementary school near Main Street and East 33rd Avenue. A 12-year-old girl reported that she was in the girls' washroom after lunch when an unknown man looked over the divider into her stall. The girl screamed and ran out of the washroom and the man ran out of the school, the release reads. The VPD says that they do not think that the man belongs to the school community. Police are releasing both video and still images of the suspect to see if someone can identify him. Investigators ask that if someone has information on who the man is they call the VPD at 604-717-0614.
